q: The Roll-on Roll-off (Ro-Ro) service of the Konkan Railway, under which loaded trucks are carried directly on railway wagons, was introduced in the year:
e: Konkan Railway introduced its Roll-on Roll-off service in 1999, carrying loaded trucks on flat wagons between Kolad and Verna, later extended to Surathkal, saving fuel and road wear.

q: The Operations Command Centre (OCC) of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, unveiled in August 2025 and described as Asia's largest rail operations control facility, is located at:
e: The WDFC Operations Command Centre unveiled in August 2025 at Sabarmati, Ahmedabad, described as Asia's largest rail operations control facility, monitors the entire 1,506 km corridor with a 72-metre video wall.

q: The headquarters of the Braithwaite, Burn and Jessop Construction Company Limited (BBJ), a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, is located at:
e: BBJ, the Braithwaite, Burn and Jessop Construction Company, a bridge-building PSU under the Ministry of Railways, has its headquarters at Kolkata.

q: The Eastern Railway was formed in April 1952 by amalgamating the Bengal Nagpur Railway with:

options.B: The remaining divisions of the East Indian Railway

e: Eastern Railway was formed on 14 April 1952 by amalgamating the Bengal Nagpur Railway with the remaining divisions of the East Indian Railway.

q: The North Eastern Railway, formed in April 1952, was created by the merger of the Oudh and Tirhut Railway with the:
e: North Eastern Railway was formed on 14 April 1952 by merging the Oudh and Tirhut Railway and the Kanpur-Barabanki Railway with the Assam Railway.

q: The Jhansi Workshop, the largest wagon periodic-overhaul workshop of Indian Railways, functions under the:
e: The Jhansi Workshop, Indian Railways' largest wagon periodic-overhaul workshop, is a North Central Railway unit located at Jhansi.

q: The Wagon Repair Workshop at Kota, which undertakes periodic overhaul of freight wagons, functions under the:
e: The Wagon Repair Workshop at Kota, which does periodic overhaul of freight wagons, is a West Central Railway unit.

q: The Wagon Repair Shop at Raipur, which undertakes repair and overhaul of freight wagons, functions under the:
e: The Wagon Repair Shop at Raipur, undertaking repair and overhaul of freight wagons, functions under South East Central Railway.

q: The mechanical workshop at Gorakhpur, which undertakes periodic overhaul of broad gauge coaches, is the main workshop of the:
e: The mechanical workshop at Gorakhpur, doing periodic overhaul of broad gauge coaches, is the main workshop of North Eastern Railway.

q: The Carriage Workshop at Jodhpur, which undertakes periodic overhaul of passenger coaches, functions under the:
e: The Carriage Workshop at Jodhpur, which undertakes periodic overhaul of passenger coaches, functions under North Western Railway.

q: The workshop at Samastipur in Bihar, which undertakes periodic overhaul of wagons, functions under the:
e: The workshop at Samastipur in Bihar, which undertakes periodic overhaul of wagons, functions under East Central Railway.

q: The Forged Wheel Plant at Lalganj, Raebareli, which manufactures forged wheels for locomotives and high-speed trains, functions as a unit of the:
e: The Forged Wheel Plant at Lalganj, Raebareli, which makes forged wheels for locomotives and high-speed trains, functions as a unit of the Modern Coach Factory, Raebareli.

q: The railway workshop at Kalka in Haryana mainly undertakes the periodic overhaul and repair of:

options.C: The narrow gauge coaches and wagons of the Kalka-Shimla Railway

e: The Kalka workshop in Haryana mainly overhauls and repairs the narrow gauge coaches and wagons of the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla Railway.

q: Before being renamed as the National Academy of Indian Railways (NAIR), the apex training academy at Vadodara was known as the:
e: The apex academy at Vadodara, now the National Academy of Indian Railways, was earlier known as the Railway Staff College, founded in 1930 and shifted to Vadodara in 1952.

q: In Indian Railways, the application 'SFOORTI', launched for freight managers to monitor freight business through GIS views, stands for:

options.A: Smart Freight Operations and Organisation of Real Time Information
options.B: Single Freight Online Operations and Rail Traffic Information
options.C: Smart Freight Operation Optimisation and Real Time Information
options.D: System for Freight Operations and Online Real Time Tracking in India

e: SFOORTI stands for Smart Freight Operation Optimisation and Real Time Information, the GIS-based application that lets freight managers track and plan freight business.

q: In Indian Railways, 'SRESTHA', the research organisation set up in 2016 to drive long-term strategic research, stands for:

options.A: Special Railway Establishment for Strategic Technology and Holistic Advancement
options.B: Strategic Research Establishment for Safety, Technology and High-speed Advancement
options.C: Special Research Establishment for Signalling, Track and Haulage Advancement
options.D: Society for Railway Engineering, Science and Technology for Holistic Advancement

e: SRESTHA stands for Special Railway Establishment for Strategic Technology and Holistic Advancement, set up in 2016 under RDSO for long-term strategic railway research.

q: In railway reservation, the abbreviation 'ERS', the slip generated for a ticket booked online, stands for:
e: ERS stands for Electronic Reservation Slip, the printout or digital slip generated for a ticket booked online through IRCTC, valid with a prescribed ID proof.

q: In railway reservation charts, the waiting list code 'RLWL' stands for:
e: RLWL stands for Remote Location Waiting List, for passengers booking from intermediate remote stations where a separate quota and waiting list are maintained.

q: In railway reservation charts, the waiting list code 'PQWL' stands for:
e: PQWL stands for Pooled Quota Waiting List, shared by passengers travelling from several intermediate stations under a common pooled quota.

q: In the integrated materials management system of Indian Railways, the module 'UDM' through which user departments draw stores stands for:
e: UDM stands for User Depot Module, the IREPS-IMMS module through which user departments place demands and draw stores from depots.

q: In Indian Railways, the system 'OMS', used by the RDSO to measure the riding quality and oscillations of vehicles on track, stands for:
e: OMS stands for Oscillation Monitoring System, used by RDSO to record ride quality and vehicle oscillations during trials and speed certification runs.

q: In LHB coach rakes of Indian Railways, the power supply system 'EOG' stands for:
e: EOG stands for End-on Generation, the system in which a power car at the end of an LHB rake generates electricity for the coaches, unlike self-generating coaches.

q: At railway stations, the enquiry terminal 'POET', through which passengers can themselves obtain train information, stands for:
e: POET stands for Passenger Operated Enquiry Terminal, the station kiosk through which passengers can themselves check train running and reservation status.

q: In the Mumbai suburban railway system, the machine 'CVM', used for validating printed coupon booklets for season and single journey tickets, stands for:
e: CVM stands for Coupon Validating Machine, used in the Mumbai suburban system to validate printed coupon booklets for season and single journey tickets before travel.

q: In Indian Railways, the designation 'TXR', borne by the staff who examine trains and certify them fit for running, stands for:
e: TXR stands for Train Examiner, the carriage and wagon staff who examine trains, rectify defects and certify rakes fit and safe for running.

q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, seven high-speed rail corridors were announced as 'growth connectors'. Which of the following pairs is NOT among these seven corridors?
e: The seven Budget 2026-27 high-speed corridors are Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri, so Delhi-Kolkata is not among them.

q: The new dedicated freight corridor announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 will connect Dankuni in West Bengal with:
e: The Union Budget 2026-27 announced a new east-west dedicated freight corridor connecting Dankuni in West Bengal with Surat in Gujarat for greener cargo movement.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor was declared fully complete on 31 March 2026 after a successful trial run on its final section between:

options.A: Jawaharlal Nehru Port and Vaitarna (New Saphale)

e: DFCCIL declared the WDFC fully complete on 31 March 2026 after a successful trial run on the final JNPT to Vaitarna (New Saphale) section, finishing the 1,506 km corridor.

q: According to the Ministry of Railways, the number of special train trips operated by Indian Railways for the Maha Kumbh between 13 January and 28 February 2025 was:
e: The Ministry of Railways recorded 17,340 special train trips operated for the Maha Kumbh between 13 January and 28 February 2025, its largest such operation in 2025.

q: As of 31 October 2025, the number of Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals commissioned by Indian Railways, against the original target of 100, was:
e: As of 31 October 2025, Indian Railways had commissioned 118 Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminals across 18 states and UTs, exceeding the original target of 100.

q: As of November 2025, the share of the broad gauge network of Indian Railways that had been electrified was about:
e: By November 2025 about 99.2 per cent of the broad gauge network had been electrified under Mission 100 per cent Electrification, making it the world's largest electrified rail network.

q: In 2024, Indian Railways approved the installation of the Kavach 4.0 automatic train protection system on how many locomotives?
e: In 2024 the government approved installing Kavach 4.0, the indigenous automatic train protection system, on 10,000 locomotives across the network.

q: The four new Amrit Bharat Express trains flagged off by the Prime Minister from Motihari in July 2025 included a service between Bapudham Motihari and:
e: Of the four Amrit Bharat Express trains flagged off from Motihari in July 2025, one ran between Bapudham Motihari and Anand Vihar Terminal, Delhi, the others serving Rajendra Nagar, Darbhanga and Malda Town routes.

q: The Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project, dedicated to the nation in June 2025, has a total length of about:
e: The Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link, dedicated in June 2025 with the Chenab and Anji bridges, is about 272 km long, connecting Kashmir by rail with the rest of India.

q: 'Operation Jeevan Raksha' of the Railway Protection Force is associated with:

options.A: Recovery of lost luggage of passengers
options.C: Saving the lives of passengers who come close to being run over by trains at platforms and on tracks
options.D: Rescue of runaway children found on railway premises

e: Operation Jeevan Raksha is the RPF drive for saving the lives of passengers who slip or fall close to being run over by trains at platforms and on tracks.

q: The Sanskrit novel 'Kadambari', one of the earliest novels of world literature, was composed by:
e: Kadambari, the Sanskrit prose romance regarded as one of the world's earliest novels, was composed by Banabhatta, court poet of Harshavardhana, and completed by his son.

q: The Sanskrit play 'Mrichchhakatika' (The Little Clay Cart) is attributed to:
e: Mrichchhakatika, the Sanskrit play The Little Clay Cart mixing love, politics and a courtroom trial, is attributed to King Shudraka.

q: The Hindi novel 'Chandrakanta', famous for its tale of romance and sorcery, was written by:
e: Chandrakanta (1888), the hugely popular Hindi novel of romance, tilism and sorcery that taught many readers the Devanagari script, was written by Devaki Nandan Khatri.

q: The philosophical work 'The Republic', written in the form of dialogues, was authored by:
e: The Republic, Plato's dialogue on justice and the ideal state, presents the philosopher-king and the allegory of the cave through Socrates.

q: The book 'Utopia', describing an ideal island society, was written by:
e: Utopia (1516), describing an ideal island society with common property, was written by Thomas More, who coined the word utopia itself.

q: The Russian novel 'Dead Souls', a satire on provincial landowners, was written by:
e: Dead Souls (1842), Nikolai Gogol's satire in which Chichikov buys the names of dead serfs, exposes the greed of provincial Russian landowners.

q: The novel in verse 'Eugene Onegin', a classic of Russian literature, was written by:
e: Eugene Onegin, the novel in verse considered a foundation of modern Russian literature, was written by Alexander Pushkin.

q: The adventure novel 'The Call of the Wild', set in the Canadian Yukon, was written by:
e: The Call of the Wild (1903), Jack London's adventure novel about the sled dog Buck in the Klondike gold rush in the Canadian Yukon, made him famous.

q: The novel 'Lord of the Flies', about schoolboys stranded on an uninhabited island, was written by:
e: Lord of the Flies (1954), about schoolboys stranded on an uninhabited island who descend into savagery, was written by William Golding.

q: The children's fantasy novel 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe', the first published book of the Narnia series, was written by:
e: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (1950), the first published Chronicle of Narnia introducing Aslan and the White Witch, was written by C. S. Lewis.

q: The children's book 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory', featuring the chocolatier Willy Wonka, was written by:
e: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (1964), Roald Dahl's children's classic, follows Charlie Bucket's tour of Willy Wonka's chocolate factory.

q: The dystopian novel 'Fahrenheit 451', set in a society where books are burnt, was written by:
e: Fahrenheit 451 (1953), Ray Bradbury's dystopian novel of a society where firemen burn books, is named after the temperature at which book paper burns.

q: The novel 'Things Fall Apart', depicting the impact of colonialism on Igbo society in Nigeria, was written by:
e: Things Fall Apart (1958), Chinua Achebe's novel about Okonkwo and the impact of colonialism and missionaries on Igbo society in Nigeria, is a landmark of African literature.

q: The novella 'The Little Prince', a poetic tale narrated by a stranded pilot, was written by:
e: The Little Prince (1943), the poetic novella narrated by a pilot stranded in the Sahara, was written by French aviator-author Antoine de Saint-Exupery.

q: The novel 'Siddhartha', set in India in the time of Gautama Buddha, was written by:
e: Siddhartha (1922), Hermann Hesse's novel of a young man's spiritual journey in India in the time of Gautama Buddha, reflects the author's deep interest in Indian philosophy.

q: The play 'Peter Pan', about the boy who would not grow up, was written by:
e: Peter Pan, the boy who never grows up, was created by Scottish author J. M. Barrie, first in the 1904 play Peter Pan, or The Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up.

q: The book 'Walden', an account of the author's life in a cabin beside Walden Pond, was written by:
e: Walden (1854) is Henry David Thoreau's account of his two years living in a self-built cabin on Walden Pond in Massachusetts, reflecting on simple living and nature.

q: The Fourteenth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Fourteenth Finance Commission, which recommended the devolution of taxes for 2015-20, was chaired by former RBI Governor Y. V. Reddy.

q: The Seventh Central Pay Commission, constituted in 2014, was chaired by:
e: The Seventh Central Pay Commission, constituted in February 2014 to revise pay of central government employees, was chaired by Justice A. K. Mathur.

q: The Health Survey and Development Committee (1943), which laid the foundation of India's health policy, was chaired by:
e: The Health Survey and Development Committee of 1943, whose report shaped India's health policy and planning, was chaired by Sir Joseph Bhore and is known as the Bhore Committee.

q: The Lakdawala Committee (1993) is best known for its work on the:
e: The Lakdawala Committee of 1993, headed by D. T. Lakdawala, is known for its methodology for estimating poverty and the poverty line in India.

q: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (2004) was chaired by:
e: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, set up in 2004, was chaired by economist Arjun Sengupta.

q: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) on black money, constituted in 2014, was chaired by:
e: The Special Investigation Team on black money, constituted in 2014 following a Supreme Court direction, was chaired by Justice M. B. Shah.

q: The Justice Mudgal Committee (2013) was appointed to inquire into:

options.A: The administration of the Board of Control for Cricket in India
options.C: Allegations of betting and spot-fixing in the Indian Premier League

e: The Justice Mudgal Committee of 2013, headed by Justice Mukul Mudgal, inquired into allegations of betting and spot-fixing in the Indian Premier League.

q: The first National Police Commission (1977) was chaired by:
e: The first National Police Commission, set up in 1977 to review the police system, was chaired by Dharam Vira.

q: The High-Level Committee (2013) on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities was chaired by:
e: The High-Level Committee of 2013 on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities was chaired by Prof. Virginius Xaxa.

q: The Economic Administrative Reforms Commission (1981) was chaired by:
e: The Economic Administrative Reforms Commission, set up in 1981, was chaired by L. K. Jha.

q: The Reserve Bank of India Committee on Deepening of Digital Payments (2019) was chaired by:
e: The RBI Committee on Deepening of Digital Payments, constituted in 2019, was chaired by Nandan Nilekani.

q: A manometer is an instrument used to measure the:
e: A manometer measures the pressure of a gas or vapour, typically by balancing it against a column of liquid such as mercury or water.

q: A tachometer is an instrument used to measure the:

options.D: Speed of rotation of a shaft or wheel

e: A tachometer measures the speed of rotation of a shaft, wheel or engine, usually expressed in revolutions per minute.

q: An electrocardiograph (ECG) is used to record the:

options.C: Pressure of blood in the veins

e: An electrocardiograph (ECG) records the electrical activity of the heart over time through electrodes placed on the skin.

q: Indian Navy Day is celebrated every year on:
e: Indian Navy Day is observed on 4 December, commemorating Operation Trident, the Navy's attack on Karachi harbour during the 1971 war.

q: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) is located at:
e: The headquarters of SAARC, the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation founded in 1985, is located at Kathmandu in Nepal.

q: The headquarters of the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Secretariat is located at:
e: The ASEAN Secretariat is headquartered at Jakarta, Indonesia, where it has been based since the bloc's early years.

q: The capital of Turkey is:
e: Ankara is the capital of Turkey; Istanbul is its largest city but ceased to be the capital when Ankara was chosen in 1923.

q: The capital of Brazil is:
e: Brasilia, inaugurated in 1960, is the capital of Brazil; Rio de Janeiro was the earlier capital and Sao Paulo is the largest city.

q: The Statue of Unity, the tallest statue in the world, dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is located in the State of:
e: The Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue at 182 metres, dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, stands near Kevadia in Gujarat.

q: The Atal Tunnel, inaugurated in October 2020, has been built under the:
e: The Atal Tunnel, inaugurated in October 2020, is built under the Rohtang Pass and connects Manali with the Lahaul-Spiti valley in Himachal Pradesh.

q: Dr. Salim Ali, one of India's most celebrated ornithologists, is popularly known as the:
e: Dr. Salim Ali, the celebrated ornithologist who surveyed birds across India, is popularly known as the Birdman of India.

q: Mount Everest was first climbed in 1953 by Edmund Hillary together with:
e: Mount Everest was first climbed on 29 May 1953 by Edmund Hillary of New Zealand together with Sherpa Tenzing Norgay.

q: Which is the most populous State of India?
e: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous State of India, with a population of over 19.9 crore as per the 2011 Census, ahead of Maharashtra and Bihar.

q: The Olympic symbol, displayed on the Olympic flag, consists of how many interlaced rings?
e: The Olympic symbol consists of five interlaced rings in blue, yellow, black, green and red, representing the inhabited continents.

q: Numismatics is the branch of study that deals with:
e: Numismatics is the study and collection of coins, currency and medals.

q: The 'Baht' is the currency of:
e: The Baht is the currency of Thailand; Vietnam uses the dong, Malaysia the ringgit and Indonesia the rupiah.

q: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an international tournament in the game of:
e: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an annual international men's field hockey tournament held in Malaysia.

q: Kutch Railway Company Limited, a joint venture led by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), was set up primarily for which project?

options.A: Gauge conversion of the Gandhidham-Palanpur railway line
options.B: Construction of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor in Gujarat
options.C: Gauge conversion of the Bharuch-Dahej railway line
options.D: Development of a new port rail link to Mundra

e: Kutch Railway Company Limited, an RVNL-led joint venture, was set up for the gauge conversion of the Gandhidham-Palanpur railway line in Gujarat.

q: Bharuch Dahej Railway Company Limited was incorporated as a special purpose vehicle (SPV) for the gauge conversion of which railway line?
e: Bharuch Dahej Railway Company Limited was incorporated as an SPV for the gauge conversion of the Bharuch-Dahej railway line connecting the Dahej port and industrial area.

q: Krishnapatnam Railway Company Limited, a joint venture of RVNL, was formed to construct a new broad gauge line from Obulavaripalle to which place?
e: Krishnapatnam Railway Company Limited, an RVNL joint venture, was formed to build the new broad gauge line from Obulavaripalle to Krishnapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh.

q: Hassan Mangalore Rail Development Company Limited is a joint venture of the Ministry of Railways with the Government of which State?
e: Hassan Mangalore Rail Development Company Limited is a joint venture of the Ministry of Railways with the Government of Karnataka for the Hassan-Mangaluru line.

q: RailTel Enterprises Limited, formerly a wholly owned subsidiary of RailTel Corporation of India Limited (amalgamated with RailTel with effect from 27 September 2023), was incorporated in which year?
e: RailTel Enterprises Limited, the former wholly owned subsidiary of RailTel that was amalgamated with RailTel with effect from 27 September 2023, was incorporated on 12 August 2014.

q: Ircon Infrastructure and Services Limited (IrconISL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of which company?
e: Ircon Infrastructure and Services Limited (IrconISL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Ircon International Limited, engaged in infrastructure and related services.

q: Fresh and Healthy Enterprises Limited (FHEL), which operates in the cold chain logistics segment, is a wholly owned subsidiary of which railway PSU?
e: Fresh and Healthy Enterprises Limited (FHEL), which operates in the cold chain logistics segment, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Container Corporation of India (CONCOR).

q: Angul Sukinda Railway Limited, an SPV created through RVNL for a new line linking the Talcher coal and iron ore belt, is executing its project in which State?
e: Angul Sukinda Railway Limited, an RVNL SPV for the Angul-Sukinda new line linking the Talcher coal and iron ore belt, executes its project in Odisha.

q: In the Gujarat Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (G-RIDE), the majority equity partner is the:
e: In Gujarat Rail Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (G-RIDE), the Government of Gujarat is the majority equity partner, with the Ministry of Railways holding the balance.

q: 'iPay', launched in February 2019, is the own payment gateway of which railway organisation?

options.C: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)

e: iPay, launched in February 2019, is the in-house payment gateway of IRCTC, developed for payments on its ticketing and tourism platforms.

q: Mahanadi Coal Railway Limited was incorporated mainly to develop rail infrastructure for evacuation of coal from which coalfield area?
e: Mahanadi Coal Railway Limited was incorporated to develop rail infrastructure for evacuation of coal from the Talcher coalfields in Odisha.

q: Who holds the majority equity of 64 per cent in Jharkhand Central Railway Limited?
e: In Jharkhand Central Railway Limited, Central Coalfields Limited holds the majority equity of 64 per cent, with Railways at 26 per cent and the Government of Jharkhand at 10 per cent.

q: Chhattisgarh East Railway Limited is executing the Kharsia-Dharamjaygarh rail project primarily for evacuation of coal from which coalfield area?
e: Chhattisgarh East Railway Limited is executing the Kharsia-Dharamjaygarh rail project primarily for evacuation of coal from the Mand-Raigarh coalfields.

q: South Eastern Railway came into existence in which year, when the Bengal Nagpur Railway portion was separated from Eastern Railway?
e: South Eastern Railway came into existence in 1955, when the Bengal Nagpur Railway portion was separated from Eastern Railway.

q: North Central Railway came into existence on which date?
e: North Central Railway, headquartered at Prayagraj, came into existence on 1 April 2003.

q: The railway workshop at Dibrugarh, which undertakes periodic overhaul of coaches and wagons, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The railway workshop at Dibrugarh in Assam, which undertakes periodic overhaul of coaches and wagons, belongs to Northeast Frontier Railway.

q: The Central Workshop at Ashokapuram, Mysuru, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Central Workshop at Ashokapuram, Mysuru, functions under South Western Railway, whose headquarters is at Hubballi.

q: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Lower Parel in Mumbai belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Lower Parel in Mumbai belongs to Western Railway.

q: The Locomotive Workshop at Charbagh, Lucknow is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Locomotive Workshop at Charbagh, Lucknow is administered by Northern Railway.

q: The railway workshop at Amritsar functions under which zonal railway?
e: The railway workshop at Amritsar functions under Northern Railway, in whose Firozpur division Amritsar is located.
